# Recipe page shows the ingredients first

## Problem Statement

Home cooks open a recipe on their phone while standing in the kitchen, often on a weak mobile connection. Today the recipe page loads the full photo gallery, the comments and the video player before the ingredient list appears, so the cook waits with nothing to read. The parent vision's analytics show that 38 percent of mobile visitors leave a recipe page before it finishes loading, and support mail names slowness as the most common complaint.

## Business Alignment

**Job to Be Done:** When I am standing in my kitchen with a recipe open on my phone over a weak mobile connection, I want to see the ingredient list before the photos, comments and video have loaded, so I can start gathering ingredients instead of waiting with nothing to read.

**Impact Map:**
- **Goal:** Fewer mobile visitors leave a recipe page before they can read it (parent vision success criterion). Baseline from the vision's analytics: 38 percent of mobile visitors leave before the page finishes loading.
- **Actor:** A home cook reading a recipe on a phone, usually over a mobile data connection (the parent vision's target audience).
- **Impact:** The cook starts reading the ingredient list while the photos, comments and video are still loading, instead of leaving the page. You can see this as fewer mobile visitors leaving the recipe page before they can read it, compared with the 38 percent baseline. The owner sets the target figure (see Business Risks).
- **Deliverable:** A phone recipe page that shows the recipe title and the complete ingredient list without waiting for photos, comments or video, and keeps the list in place when they arrive.

## User Stories

**Story 1: Read the ingredients first.** **As a** home cook reading a recipe on my phone over mobile data, **I want** the recipe title and the complete ingredient list displayed without waiting for the photos, comments and video, **so that** I can start gathering ingredients instead of waiting with nothing to read. (Scenarios 1-3)

**Story 2: Keep the media and my place.** **As a** home cook reading a recipe on my phone over mobile data, **I want** the photos, comments and video to still arrive on the same page without moving the ingredient list I am reading, **so that** seeing the ingredients first costs me neither the gallery, comments and video nor my place in the list. (Scenarios 4-5)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Scenario 1: Ingredient list displayed before any media has loaded** (Story 1, happy path)
  Given a recipe that has a photo gallery, comments and a video
  And a cook opens it on a phone whose connection has not yet delivered any photo, comment or video
  When the recipe page has opened
  Then the recipe title and the ingredient list are displayed on the page
  And each ingredient line shows the quantity, unit and ingredient name the author entered
  And this holds while no photo, comment or video has finished loading

- [ ] **Scenario 2: Photos, comments and video fail to load** (Story 1, error path)
  Given a cook has opened a recipe page on a phone and the ingredient list is displayed
  When the photos, the comments and the video all fail to load, because the connection drops or their source returns an error
  Then the recipe title and every ingredient line stay displayed
  And no spinner, error message or empty media frame is drawn over any ingredient line

- [ ] **Scenario 3: Ingredient list longer than one phone screen** (Story 1, edge case)
  Given a recipe whose ingredient list is longer than one phone screen
  And no photo, comment or video of that recipe has finished loading
  When the cook scrolls through the ingredient list
  Then every ingredient line of the recipe is displayed, none missing, in the order the author entered them

- [ ] **Scenario 4: Photos, comments and video still arrive** (Story 2, happy path)
  Given a cook has the recipe page open on a phone with a working connection, and the ingredient list is displayed
  When the cook scrolls to where the photo gallery, the comments and the video player belong
  Then each of the three is shown on that same page, without the cook reloading or leaving the page

- [ ] **Scenario 5: Ingredient list keeps its place when media arrives** (Story 2, edge case)
  Given a cook has an ingredient line on screen while the photo gallery, the comments or the video is still loading
  When any of them finishes loading
  Then that ingredient line stays at the same position on screen and does not move up or down

## Scope

### In Scope
- On a phone, show the recipe title and the complete ingredient list without waiting for photos, comments or video (Scenarios 1, 3)
- Keep the ingredient list displayed when photos, comments or video fail to load (Scenario 2)
- Still show the photo gallery, comments and video player on the same page after the ingredient list (Scenario 4)
- Keep the ingredient list at its position on screen when photos, comments or video finish loading (Scenario 5)

### Out of Scope
- Desktop layout: excluded by the parent vision's Scope section.
- Search page: excluded by the parent vision's Scope section.
- Recipe editor used by authors: excluded by the parent vision's Scope section.
- Moving the ingredient list above the photo gallery in the phone layout: the vision's success criterion is about not waiting, not about position on screen. No stub covers this; the owner decides whether the layout changes.
- Showing the method steps before photos, comments and video: the vision's success criteria name only the ingredient list. No stub covers this; the owner decides whether it gets one.
- Making the photos, comments or video themselves load in less time (for example smaller image files): the vision does not name this, and no stub covers it.
- A target figure for the mobile leave rate: this is a business KPI that the owner sets in the Product Loop, not in this technical pipeline (see Business Risks).

## Risks

### Technical Risks
- **Unknown load path for the ingredient list:** this project contains no recipe page source to inspect. Glob `**/*` over the project root matched 4 files: the parent vision, this plan, its status file and one agent definition. Meeting Scenario 1 could take more than a change in load order. That happens if the ingredient list arrives in the same response as the comments, or if the page draws nothing until a script that also carries the gallery and video player has loaded. In either case the ingredient data must be split from the media.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: HIGH
  - Mitigation: Trace the current recipe page's requests on a throttled phone connection before implementation planning. Record which request carries the ingredient list and what holds back its display.
- **Ingredient list jumps when media arrives:** Scenario 5 needs space held for the photo gallery, comments and video before they load. If stored photos and videos have no recorded dimensions, that space is not known in advance.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: MEDIUM
  - Mitigation: Check whether stored photos and videos carry their width and height. Have the implementation plan state how the space is held when they do not.

### Business Risks
- **No target for the leave rate:** the vision asks for fewer mobile visitors leaving (baseline 38 percent) but sets no target. Without one, nobody can say after release whether the change was enough. Choosing that number is a business KPI decision for the owner, not for this technical pipeline.
  - Likelihood: HIGH
  - Impact: MEDIUM
  - Mitigation: Ask the owner, through the Product Loop, to set the target leave rate before release.
- **Cooks may leave for reasons this plan does not touch:** the vision cites the 38 percent figure and the slowness complaints. As quoted, the analytics do not say how many of those visitors left while waiting for the ingredient list specifically.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: MEDIUM
  - Mitigation: Compare the mobile leave rate before and after release, split by whether the ingredient list was on the page when the visitor left.

### Dependency Risks
- **Measuring the effect depends on the existing analytics:** this plan does not know whether the analytics behind the 38 percent figure can tell a visitor who left before the ingredient list appeared from one who left later. The change works for the cook either way; only the measurement is affected.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: LOW
  - Mitigation: Check with whoever owns the analytics whether the current tracking records when a visitor leaves relative to the moment the ingredient list appears.
- **No dependency on other stubs:** `depends_on` is "none", and this is the vision's only stub. Glob `plans/functional/faster-recipe-pages-*.md` matched 1 file, this plan.

## Priority

**Priority: HIGH** (Score: 7/9)
- Dependency: MEDIUM (2): no other stub depends on this one and it depends on none; it is the vision's only stub.
- Business Impact: HIGH (3): it delivers the vision's success criterion directly, so a cook can read the ingredient list without waiting for photos, comments or video.
- Technical Risk: MEDIUM (2): no new technology is involved. How big the change is stays unknown until the page's current load path is traced (see Technical Risks).
